column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names a spirit from my understanding answering me; BSB says my understanding prompts a reply.
The Hebrew asks do you know, without the added not in BSB.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names his height and a cloud in the singular; BSB has arrogance and clouds.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has an active plural subject not finding him; BSB uses never to be found.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes his bones the subject of being full of youth; BSB makes youthful vigor the subject.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the palate; BSB says mouth.
The Hebrew names gall rather than venom and describes the food as changed, without the added sours.
The Hebrew narrates swallowing and vomiting as completed actions; BSB uses present verbs.
The Hebrew names a viper’s tongue; BSB says fangs.
The Hebrew says see and names butter; BSB says enjoy and cream.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a house in the singular; BSB has houses.
The Hebrew speaks of no quiet in his belly; BSB interprets this as an unsatisfied appetite.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew pictures every hand of the afflicted coming upon him; BSB says the full force of misery.
The Hebrew leaves the sender unnamed; BSB explicitly supplies God.
The Hebrew names a bronze bow; BSB says a bronze-tipped arrow.
The Hebrew has an active subject drawing it out and names gall; BSB uses a passive and says liver.
The Hebrew says the survivor in his tent will fare badly; BSB describes the fire devouring what is left.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the possessor of the wrath unnamed; BSB supplies God.
The Hebrew calls it the inheritance of His decree from God; BSB makes God explicitly the one appointing it.
